text:
support-alex: Quick escalation — OmniBank private deployment (ExpressRoute) is failing periodic control-plane syncs. Circuit shows UP and BGP established, but our control plane reports TLS client cert validation failures and customer app gets 403s when trying to pull models. Suspect provider is SNATing our source IPs on the peering path and customer FW only allows Redwood control IPs.

support-alex: Repro steps I ran from their bastion: 
```
$ curl -v --cert client.pem --key client.key https://control.private.omnibank.internal/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://control.private.omnibank.internal/health
*   Trying 203.0.113.45...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to control.private.omnibank.internal (203.0.113.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* Server certificate: CN=control.private.omnibank.internal
* client certificate selection failed: certificate unknown
* SSL: certificate subject name 'control.private.omnibank.internal' matched
* SSL: certificate verify result: certificate unknown (18), continuing anyway.
* Closing connection 0
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

```

support-alex: tcpdump on their peering interface (snippet):
```
20:11:22.123456 IP 198.51.100.23.54321 > 203.0.113.45.443: Flags [P.], seq 1234:2345, ack 5678, win 229, length 111
20:11:22.223456 IP 198.51.100.23.54321 > 203.0.113.45.443: Flags [F.], seq 2345, ack 5789, win 229, length 0
```
(note: source 198.51.100.23 is the provider NAT range; expected our control-plane source 198.51.100.5)

eng-network-jordan: Thanks Alex. Looks like the pcap shows source IP mapped to provider space. Please run these checks for me:
- `show ip bgp neighbor` on the customer router to confirm next-hop and update-source.
- `traceroute -T -p 443 control.private.omnibank.internal` from bastion and from provider PE if possible.
- capture full pcap and grep for TCP SYNs to 203.0.113.45 to see initial src.

eng-network-jordan: If provider is doing source-NAT for egress across their MPLS/edge, their NAT pool needs to be included in the customer's TLS allowlist (or we need to request they preserve original source). Also check whether a route-map on the PE is rewriting source or doing NAT64/siimilar.

support-alex: Ran `show ip bgp neighbors` on their edge -> snippet: 
```
BGP neighbor is 10.254.254.1, remote AS 65123, external link
  BGP version 4, remote router ID 10.254.254.1
  BGP state = Established, up for 02:14:23
  Network mask: 255.255.255.255
  Next hop: 198.51.100.5
```
Customer firewall ruleset (redacted) only permits src 198.51.100.5 and 203.0.113.0/24 to port 443. Provider NAT pool 198.51.100.0/24 was not on the allowlist.

eng-sre-maya: Two immediate mitigations: 
1) Have customer temporarily add provider NAT pool (198.51.100.0/24) to their FW allowlist for control-plane destination IPs. That should let the TLS sessions complete while we work with provider.
2) Longer-term: ask provider to disable source NAT for peered traffic or configure 1:1 NAT mapping to the expected Redwood source IP range, or move the peering to a sub-interface where source preservation is enforced.

eng-sre-maya: Also confirm whether mutual TLS validation is bound to source IPs (it shouldn't be). If customer policy ties client cert acceptance to src IP, recommend updating their mTLS policy to validate only cert CN/SAN and not source IP. If that's blocked by compliance, document provider NAT ranges and maintain allowlist.

support-alex: I pushed the workaround — customer added 198.51.100.0/24 to their allowlist. After that their background sync succeeded and model pulls recovered.

cust-ops: Confirmed. After adding provider pool to allowlist at 20:12 UTC, control-plane handshakes succeeded and 403s stopped. We also notified provider to investigate NAT behaviour; they're opening a ticket.

support-alex: For the record I'm asking provider for: 
- confirmation of any source NAT on ExpressRoute circuit/PE
- mapping of NAT pool -> original source if 1:1 available
- whether they can preserve source IPs for our prefixes

pd-bot: PagerDuty alert cleared (incident 8742) — escalation resolved by customer firewall change.

eng-network-jordan: Follow-up action items: 
- eng-network to own conversation with provider on NAT preservation and request config change.
- support to keep one-week monitoring; if provider cannot preserve source IPs, we should add provider NAT pools to our deployment runbooks for affected customers.

support-alex: Thanks all — closing on our side but leaving provider ticket open until they confirm a config change. :thumbsup:
